title: Top-K Popular Autocomplete Suggestions
real_world_story: Modern search bars don't just return all matches; they surface the most relevant and popular queries to the user. Each search term in the global index is associated with a popularity score based on historical search volume. When a user types a prefix, the autocomplete engine must rapidly identify all matching queries and retrieve the top-K suggestions with the highest scores to maximize the probability of a successful query.
problem_statement: Given a set of search queries and their corresponding popularity scores, implement a system that can retrieve the top-K most popular queries that start with a given prefix. If two queries have the same popularity score, the lexicographically smaller query should be prioritized.
task: For a given search prefix, return the K most popular autocomplete suggestions in descending order of popularity. If fewer than K matches exist, return all available matches.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N (number of queries) and K (the top-K limit). The next N lines each contain a string (the query) and an integer (its popularity score). The final line contains the search prefix.
output_format: A list of K (or fewer) queries, each on a new line, ordered by popularity (descending) and then lexicographically (ascending).

examples.explanation: Queries starting with 'app' are: 'app' (20), 'apple' (10), 'application' (15), 'applet' (12). The top 2 most popular are 'app' (20) and 'application' (15).

expected_algorithm: Trie + Max-Heap / Sorting of subtree results
real_world_takeaway: Combining prefix-based retrieval with weight-based ranking is the foundation of modern recommendation and autocomplete systems, ensuring users find the most relevant information with minimal keystrokes.
